The upper bound follows from the standard balanced edge-colouring theorem for bipartite graphs: with k+1 colours, d_alpha(v)<=ceil(d(v)/(k+1))<=(d(v)-1)/k for every d(v)>=k^2+1, so every edge sees at most (d(u)+d(v)-2)/k adjacent edges of any colour. For the lower bound on K_{k^2,k^2+1}, fixing one colour gives d_H(x)+d_H(y)-2*1_{xy in H}<=2k-1. Rechecking the high-vertex case split yields |E(H)|<=M_k=k^3-k^2+k: if one side has no degree-k vertex this is immediate; if both sides have high vertices, all opposite high pairs are edges, and either every high degree is k or a degree-(k+1) vertex confines every opposite vertex of degree at least k-1 to its neighborhood. The resulting two orientation bounds are k^3-2k^2+3k and k^3-2k^2+2k+2, both below M_k. Thus k+1 colours cover at most (k+1)M_k=k^4+k<k^4+k^2 edges. An independent MILP for k=2 certified the exact one-colour maximum M_2=6 with zero gap.
